landmarks.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus (Olympieion)
landmarks.why: Phaedrus has come from Epicrates' house, “the one that was Morychus’s, near the Olympieion” (227b).
landmarks.matched: OSM way/63765671: Temple of Olympian Zeus

landmarks.name: Arch of Hadrian
landmarks.why: Orientation only (AD 131/2, long after the dialogue).

landmarks.name: Temple of Apollo Delphinios (site)
landmarks.why: Pausanias 1.19.1 places it close to the Olympieion; marks the sanctuary quarter the pair walk through.
landmarks.matched: OSM way/146815833: Temple of Apollo Delphinios

landmarks.name: Church of Agia Fotini on the Ilissos
landmarks.why: Built 1872 on the river bed; the one place the Ilissos is still open to the sky in central Athens.

landmarks.name: Sanctuary of Pan (rock relief)
landmarks.why: Rock-cut sanctuary beside the church; a relief of Pan was found on the rock in 1911. Some identify this rocky stretch with the shrine of Acheloos and the Nymphs of 230b–c; others do not.

landmarks.name: The Ilissos, uncovered stretch
landmarks.why: The only section of the river mapped as not in a tunnel; everything else is culverted under streets.

landmarks.name: Temple of Artemis Agrotera (site, Agrai)
landmarks.why: Pausanias 1.19.6: “across the Ilisus is a district called Agrae and a temple of Artemis Agrotera.” Socrates at 229c: the altar of Boreas is “where you cross over to the precinct of Agra.” Demolished 1778; retaining wall found 1962.
landmarks.matched: OSM way/479255983: Temple of Artemis Agrotera

landmarks.name: Temple of Zeus Meilichios (site)
landmarks.why: A 4th-century BC temple on the Agrai bank; shows how thick with sanctuaries this side of the river was.
landmarks.matched: OSM node/9517245642: Ναός του Μειλιχίου Διός

landmarks.name: Panathenaic Stadium
landmarks.why: Built by Lykourgos c. 330 BC, so not yet there in the dialogue’s dramatic date; marks the ravine between Agra and Ardettos.
landmarks.matched: OSM relation/19023844: Panathenaic Stadium (start_date C6 BC)

landmarks.name: Ardettos hill
landmarks.why: Wycherley (1963) put the plane tree on the east bank at the foot of Ardettos.
